steps.ask: Which sets of three different digits can have a sum that is a digit from 6 to 9? How will you make sure none are missed?
steps.title: List the sets of three different digits that can add up to a digit

lines.text: The first three digits are different and add to the fourth digit, which is at most 9.
The smallest sum is $1 + 2 + 3 = 6$, so the fourth digit is 6 to 9.
There are 7 sets, and the fourth digit is always new because it is bigger than each of the three.

problems.note: This asks why a set of means is unreliable, not which display to choose, so it is the weakest fit in this batch. It keeps the reasoned judgement about whether a summary can be trusted for the data given.

steps.ask: What information about the voters is missing from Table 2, and how would that change the means?
steps.title: Explain the problem

lines.text: The means treat every age group as equal, but the groups did not have equal numbers of voters.
Table 2 gives percentages only. The number of voters in each age group is not used, so the means are unreliable.
The real result (Table 1) was Leave 52%, so the Remain mean of 52.33% does not reflect the outcome.

problems.final: \hl{1}{\text{The number of voters in each age group is not used, so the means are unreliable.}}

steps.ask: What are the lowest and highest rates before exercise, and after exercise, and how far apart are they each time?

lines.text: Before exercise the rates run from $60$ to $89$, a range of $\hl{1}{29}$.
After exercise they run from $71$ to $118$, a range of $\hl{1}{47}$.
The after-exercise values are more spread out, so the standard deviation increased.

lines.text: Categorical data is sorted into groups, not counted or measured. It is ordinal if the groups have a natural order and nominal if they do not.
